Photonic Packaging Engineer

About Quandela

Quandela is a global leader in photonic quantum computing, developing hardware and software technologies to build scalable and energy-efficient quantum systems.

With more than 140 people, we develop our own stack, from semiconductor quantum emitters and photonic integrated circuits to quantum control systems, software and algorithms.

Our ambition is to build large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers. Reaching this scale requires increasingly reliable, manufacturable and integrated photonic hardware, making our Integrated Photonics team a key part of this journey.

About this position:

You will join our Integrated Photonics team, working across Massy and Palaiseau at the interface between PIC design, characterization, packaging and system integration.

We are looking for a hands-on Photonic Packaging Engineer to take ownership of our packaging activities, improve existing processes and help make our PIC integration more reliable and reproducible.

Your first priority will be to contribute to ongoing packaging activities, develop and improve assembly processes, and troubleshoot integration challenges alongside our PIC design and characterization teams.

As you grow into the role, you will also have the opportunity to develop new packaging approaches, coordinate technical projects and contribute to building more structured and scalable packaging capabilities.

Why this role matters:

Today, packaging activities involve several members of our team. Having a dedicated engineer will help us accelerate ongoing developments, improve the reproducibility of our processes and strengthen the connection between PIC design, characterization and system integration.

As our PIC platforms evolve, your work will also contribute to developing new integration approaches and preparing our packaging processes for future scale-up.

Requirements

What will you do:

Develop and improve photonic packaging processes:

• Take ownership of ongoing packaging activities and improve existing processes.
• Develop optical coupling, precision alignment and fiber-array attachment methods.
• Work on component assembly, bonding and electrical interconnections.
• Address mechanical and thermal integration challenges.
• Test new approaches, troubleshoot issues and improve process reproducibility.

Qualify and improve packaged devices:

• Build and test prototypes to validate packaging approaches.
• Define performance metrics, tolerances and acceptance criteria.
• Characterize packaged PICs alongside the PIC Characterization team.
• Troubleshoot optical, electrical and mechanical integration issues.
• Establish repeatable procedures and technical documentation.

Connect packaging with PIC design:

• Work closely with PIC Designers to anticipate packaging constraints.
• Translate assembly challenges into practical design-for-packaging guidelines.
• Collaborate with characterization and system-integration teams to improve packaged device performance.

Build the packaging capability:

• Collaborate with external packaging partners and equipment suppliers.
• Improve existing equipment, assembly methods and internal capabilities.
• Explore new packaging technologies and integration approaches.
• Support automation to improve accuracy, reproducibility and throughput.
• Progressively lead technical projects and contribute to future scale-up.

How you'll grow:

0–3 months → Get familiar with our PIC platforms, existing packaging processes and integration challenges. Contribute to ongoing activities and start taking ownership of selected technical tasks.

3–6 months → Take increasing responsibility for packaging processes, develop and test improvements, and contribute to making our assembly methods more reliable and reproducible.

6–12 months → Lead packaging development activities within your area of expertise, strengthen our qualification and documentation practices, and contribute to new packaging approaches and technical projects.

Longer term → Depending on your experience and interests, grow into a broader technical role, leading packaging projects, strengthening external partnerships and helping shape our future packaging capabilities.

--

What we're looking for:

Must-have:

• Master's or PhD in Photonics, Physics, Engineering, Microelectronics or related fields.
• Hands-on experience in photonic, optoelectronic or semiconductor packaging.
• Practical experience in optical alignment, component assembly or related processes.
• Good understanding of packaging tolerances, process development and qualification.
• Ability to troubleshoot integration issues and develop reliable packaging solutions.
• Professional English.

Important, but you can grow here

• Fiber-array / FAU attachment and fiber-to-chip coupling
• Wire bonding, flip-chip integration or other electrical interconnection techniques.
• Design for packaging, assembly and manufacturability
• Mechanical and thermal integration
• Experience working with external packaging suppliers or technology partners
• Automation of packaging or precision-assembly processes

Bonus

• Packaging of integrated photonic devices
• Experience with active photonic or optoelectronic components.
• Cryogenic packaging
• High-density electrical interconnection
• Semiconductor production, process-engineering or NPI experience
• Experience developping packaging equipment
• Previous experience coordinating technical projects or leading packaging development activities.

> You do not need previous experience in quantum computing.

> What matters most is your ability to work hands-on with packaging processes, understand integration challenges and help us develop reliable and reproducible solutions.

Benefits

Join a growing quantum hardware company and contribute directly to the development of next-generation photonic quantum processors.

• Take ownership of key PIC packaging activities and processes.
• Develop reliable and reproducible packaging solutions.
• Grow your expertise and contribute to future packaging developments.
• Collaborate with PIC design, characterization and integration teams.

Where our previous interns work now

After Tacto, over 10 former interns have founded their own companies, with e.g. 3 already going through Y Combinator. Others have joined programs like CDTM (5+ acceptances), moved into top consulting firms, or joined early-stage startups and VCs. The common thread: they all got a real understanding of what it takes to build and scale a company.

 

Our Background

Tacto is building the intelligence layer that connects AI to the physical world of manufacturing, starting with procurement. AI is transforming every industry, but it stops at the factory gate. The knowledge that holds manufacturing together - part costs, suppliers, materials - is scattered across systems and people. Over 50% of a product's cost originates from suppliers, making procurement the single largest cost lever in manufacturing and the missing connection between the digital and the physical world. Yet it still runs on Excel and legacy systems. We're changing that with our Procurement Intelligence Platform, trusted by hundreds of companies running billions of Euros of material.

Based in Munich, we are 100+ passionate builders who are in-office, with high expectations, fast growth, and a lot of fun. We are supported by >€50m from Sequoia, Index, and Europe's leading tech entrepreneurs and industry veterans.

Why It Matters

Manufacturing forms Europe's economic backbone, driving a fourth of Europe's GDP and providing over 30% of jobs. These hidden champions and global market leaders manufacture the physical world around us, from the machines that build our cities to the medical devices that save lives.

But the world is changing. The US dominates the digital world of bits. China is scaling the world of atoms, manufacturing at unprecedented speed and scale. Geopolitics are more uncertain than ever. Europe's strength lies in its deep industrial knowledge through generations of engineering. Manufacturing worldwide runs on European machines and software. But that heritage is only an advantage if we leverage it in the age of AI.

Tacto builds the AI that connects Atoms and Bits, empowering our Industrial Base to Stay Stronger and building a lighthouse for European tech.

What We Offer

The people at Tacto are passionate about building the organization, growing themselves, and our product while having fun and being real. We have high expectations, great talent density, and a culture where your ambition, performance, and agency are what count - not where you come from or how big your ego is. You'll grow at the forefront of AI, have real ownership and impact, and be surrounded by the best people in their field who challenge you and make you better every day. That is demanding and rewarding, but that's where we thrive. Besides that you have:

  • Money: Competitive salary & equity in the company with real upside, so you are invested in our success

  • Workplace: A vibrant in-office culture (> 4 days/week) in a beautiful office in central Munich

  • Development: A development budget and regular exposure to exceptional people, e.g., Lunch & Learns, peer mentoring, external speakers

  • Time off: 26 + 4 vacation days per year (4 fixed “company rest days”) as well as regular off-sites and team events

  • Health: Wellpass membership, of course, a fruit basket (!), and access to Jobrad, for your health

  • Family & Social Security: Voluntary pension contribution, voluntary KITA subsidy for your children

Please do not submit personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership, data concerning your health, or data concerning your sexual orientation.

jobs.title: Clinical Project Manager / Senior Clinical Project Manager
Content Operations Associate
jobs.description:
Content Operations Associate

Hi 👋 I'm Deyan, Director of Corporate Marketing at hyperexponential.

I lead Corporate Marketing: brand creative and design, PR and communications, flagship events, and owned media. We partner with teams across the business to produce a high volume of long-form and short-form content. A podcast episode or a report becomes clips, articles, exec posts, and social across everything the department touches.

I'm hiring a Content Operations Associate to help turn that into a repeatable operation. You'll build the pipelines that carry our content from raw material to published output, run them day to day, and make each cycle better than the last. You'll work across every part of the department rather than sitting inside one slice of it.

It's an operations role, not a strategy one. That's deliberate. You'll be close to the editorial thinking without owning it, and your job is the machinery underneath. If that's the kind of problem you want to solve, I'd love to hear from you.

About hyperexponential (hx)

At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a £7 trillion industry: which risks to take and how to price them. These decisions shape real-world outcomes. Whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.

Until now, insurance has made billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision, helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.

Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally. We're already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.

What began as a single product in one market has evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do. From building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.

What makes hx different is the people who build it. Impact isn't tied to title or tenure. It's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.

If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

About the team

Marketing at hx builds authority and demand in a niche, technically complex space. This isn't volume-driven marketing. It's deliberate, high-quality work where every output is expected to earn its place.

This role sits in Corporate Marketing: brand, content, flagship events, PR and comms, design and multimedia, and owned media. We partner with teams across the business to produce a high volume of long-form and short-form content. The opportunity now is to turn that into a repeatable operation. The pipelines that take a podcast episode or a report and turn it into clips, articles, exec posts and social. You'll help build those pipelines, run them day to day, and make each cycle better than the last.

It's an operations role rather than a strategy one. You'll be close to the editorial thinking and pick up plenty of it, but your job is the machinery that carries it.

Check out our Marketing & GTM Engineering Candidate Hub for a behind the scenes look at the team you would be joining.

What you'll be doing

Map how hx's content actually gets made. The tools, the sequence, the hand-offs, and where it breaks. Keep that picture current as the operation changes around it.

Run the production cycle across our content programmes (customer stories, the podcast, thought leadership and executive comms). Brief our agency partners, hold the quality bar on what comes back, and hit the publish dates. Take a growing share of that work in-house as you learn how it runs.

Draft copy for new web pages and projects. We draft with Claude against a codified brand voice, so you're never starting from blank. Work with input from internal SMEs and run the loop between programme owners, designers and agency partners. Brief in, feedback consolidated, builds QA'd, pages live on the date agreed.

Keep the hx thought leadership calendar operationally sound. Set the schedule, make the call on what runs when, chase the drafts, and cut existing long-form into the clips, posts and articles that feed our channels.

Keep the operations behind our named-voice programme running. The scheduling, the queue, the approvals, the chasing. So the experts and execs who carry our thought leadership post on cadence without having to manage the process themselves.

Build the templates, prompts and share packs the wider team publishes from. Good work shouldn't depend on you being available.

Learn how we stay visible in AI-generated answers as well as search results. Work out how that content gets published and distributed across the blog and website.

You'll start by running these cycles with support. Within a year we'd expect you to own them end to end and have a view on what we build next.

What we're looking for

  • You'll need to take on ownership and responsibility from the start, whatever your level. We care more about how you work than how long you've worked, and we don't expect you to have done all of this before.

  • You've made and published something (a newsletter, a channel, a society page, client work) and found yourself more interested in how it got made than in the making.

  • You're organised in a way other people can see. You track what's outstanding, you follow up, and you flag problems early rather than absorbing them.

  • You use AI properly in your own work. Reusable prompts and templates that make a recurring task faster, not a tool you tried once.

  • You pick things up by using them rather than waiting to be trained.

  • Familiarity with a CMS, a scheduling tool, or a project tracker.

  • Bonus points if you've got work out of someone you couldn't instruct (an agency, a freelancer, a collaborator) by writing a clear ask and going back when it wasn't right.

You're unlikely to thrive here if

  • You expect full product maturity, clear roadmaps, and well-defined processes before taking action - hx moves fast and requires comfort operating in ambiguity where products, priorities, and messaging are still evolving.

  • You focus primarily on flashy launch work or brand campaigns rather than the detail-oriented, outcomes-driven work of deepening adoption, engagement, and user understanding.

  • You struggle to prioritise or make trade-offs without perfect information, waiting for others to decide rather than using judgment to move work forward with the context available.

If reading our Culture Document leaves you feeling neutral rather than energised, hx may not be the place where you'll do your best work. We're building something that asks for commitment and conviction, and we want you to feel excited by the opportunity to grow with us.

Compensation

At hx, we're committed to salary transparency. You'll always have clarity on pay early in the process. Our Talent Partner will share details with you during initial conversations. We're working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally.

Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make.

Equity: We offer equity across all roles at hx, making it a significant component of total compensation. Your Talent Partner will be able to share more details about this.

Benefits

Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry.

Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together.

Our commitment to Diversity

hxers are at the centre of everything we build. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive.

Diversity is not just the right thing to do. It's key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure.

If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team.

jobs.title: Product Engineer (Senior)
jobs.description:
Product Engineer (Senior)

📍London/ Hybrid
£80,000 - £115,000 + £30,000 share options + Benefits

💬 Accurx is where conversations happen with and about patients.

For decades, the NHS has struggled with fragmented systems that make simple tasks feel impossible. We’re changing that by building a single, system-wide platform that connects everyone through communication.

What started as a way for GPs to text a patient has now evolved into an all-in-one digital toolkit used by 98% of GP practices.

Our platform now powers Total Triage to manage patient demand, and Self-Book, which lets patients schedule their own appointments in seconds. We’ve automated routine care with Patient Questionnaires for long-term conditions, while Accumail finally allows staff-to-staff communication to happen instantly across different care settings. We’re now pushing the boundaries of the consultation itself with Accurx Scribe, our AI-powered note-taker that drafts medical notes in real-time.


The team

Our engineers have sat in GP waiting rooms. They've watched practice managers juggle three systems at once to send a single message to a patient. They build for that person.

What sets our Product Engineers apart is that they own the problem, not just the code. They shape what gets built and how - working with Product, Design and Clinical from the earliest stages - and they stay with the systems they build as they evolve. They bring engineering judgment into product decisions, and product thinking into engineering ones.

Our stack is primarily C# on the backend, TypeScript and React on the frontend, running on Azure. ML/AI work uses Python. We don't expect you to know all of it - we expect you to follow a problem wherever it leads.

What you'll be doing

  • Owning features end-to-end: from refining the problem with clinicians and product managers through to architecture, implementation, rollout, and long-term evolution

  • Engaging directly with NHS GPs, practice staff and patients to build a genuine understanding of the problems you're solving — research sessions, visiting practices

  • Designing architecture and API boundaries with the broader system in mind, not just the immediate surface

  • Holding the quality bar for what you ship: not just that the code works, but that the product is reliable, intuitive and safe in a clinical context

  • Making the architectural calls that keep our codebase sustainable — improving system health alongside shipping features, not instead of it

  • Pushing back constructively when something is wrong, and committing fully when a decision has been made

What experience you need to be successful

  • Comfortable building production software across the stack - you might be strongest in backend or frontend, but you can follow a problem across both to own a feature end-to-end

  • Proven ability to reason about systems - breaking ambiguous problems into tractable pieces, spotting trade-offs and second-order effects before they become incidents

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and early-stage problem definition; you shape the work rather than wait for a finished spec

  • You treat engineering quality as part of the job - managing technical debt pragmatically, reviewing AI-generated output critically, and pushing for the right architectural decisions under real constraints

  • Curiosity about AI tools and how they change the way you work, with the judgment to know when to rely on them and when not to

What we’re looking for to demonstrate as a Product Engineer at Accurx

  • You start from the user problem, not the technology. You know what to build, what not to build, and why. In the AI era, that also means knowing what to delegate, what needs human judgment, and what shouldn't exist at all.

  • You can break ambiguous problems into tractable pieces and see how those pieces connect across boundaries. You spot seams, trade-offs, and second-order effects — thinking both from big to small and small to big.

  • You can pick up unfamiliar code, systems, and assess AI-generated output. You spot flaws before being told, and you understand why something is wrong.

  • You have strong expertise in at least one area and can use it to build, debug, and improve real systems effectively. You know what “great” looks like in your domain and can reliably get there.

  • You own outcomes, not just tasks. You influence across teams, navigate disagreement to reach the right answer, own your mistakes, and push hard for the wins that matter.

  • You actively experiment with AI tools to push the boundaries of what's possible today, with the scepticism to avoid overhyping what they can do.

  • You're actively learning and experimenting with AI tools, pushing the boundary of what's possible today, with the healthy scepticism that keeps you from overhyping what they can do.

What’s in it for me?

You'll be joining an established but fast-growing Tech for Good movement, where we're led by our Principles and our mission to fix healthcare communication.

  • £80,000 - £115,000 salary + £30,000 share options

  • Benefits to suit you: adjust your healthcare cover, your pension or life insurance, whatever stage you’re at in life

  • Flexible working: We are an office-first,, culture and ask that you’re in our (dog-friendly) Shoreditch office 3 days a week, with core hours of 10am - 4pm

  • Time off: You’ll get 28 days of holiday (plus bank holidays) and up to 4 weeks to work from anywhere per year

  • Family matters: We offer enhanced parental leave, fertility support and parental loss support

  • We have our very own Chef! Free healthy breakfasts, snacks and lunches will be provided, with the occasional sweet treat!

Compensation: £80K – £115K • Offers Equity

  • Senior • £80K – £115K • Offers Equity

jobs.title: FPGA Engineer - Electronic Warfare
jobs.description:
FPGA Engineer - Electronic Warfare

About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

Role & Mission

  • Own the development of FPGA functions for our electronic warfare and signals intelligence capabilities, from initial architecture to validation on operational hardware.

  • Work with systems and algorithm engineers to define processing requirements and assess implementation feasibility.

  • Build RTL modules in VHDL or SystemVerilog to process digitized RF signals, extract relevant information, and generate waveforms.

  • Adapt and validate DSP algorithms for FPGA implementation, balancing numerical accuracy, processing speed, and hardware resources.

  • Integrate acquisition and processing chains, including digital down-conversion, filtering, channelization, FFT, detection, direction-finding, and classification.

  • Establish verification methods and testbenches to check functional behavior and performance throughout development.

  • Connect programmable logic to RF converters and embedded processors, defining data transfers, control interfaces, clocking, and synchronization.

  • Resolve implementation constraints, achieve timing closure, and optimize resource utilization and power consumption.

  • Bring up FPGA designs on target boards, investigate integration issues, and correlate measured behavior with simulation results.

  • Contribute to laboratory and field testing alongside RF, software, and systems engineers.

  • Maintain clear design records, interface specifications, and validation evidence.

  • Improve reusable FPGA components and development practices as the product portfolio grows.

Candidate Profile

  • MSc in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Signal Processing, or a related field.

  • Strong experience developing and verifying RTL in VHDL or SystemVerilog, with a focus on digital signal processing.

  • Practical experience implementing designs on SoC FPGAs, including synthesis, implementation, timing analysis, and hardware debugging.

  • Strong understanding of sampled signals, frequency conversion, digital filtering, spectral analysis, and fixed-point numerical behavior.

  • Ability to reason across FPGA, processor, and RF hardware boundaries when making design decisions.

  • Experience modelling algorithms and comparing reference models with hardware results; familiarity with MATLAB, Simulink, Python, or HLS is a plus.

  • Familiarity with RF measurements and laboratory equipment, including spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and oscilloscopes, is a plus.

  • Prior experience in electronic warfare is welcome but not required.


Skills & Qualities

  • Hands-on engineer who enjoys taking designs from simulation to working hardware.

  • Methodical approach to debugging, with the ability to isolate problems across complex signal chains.

  • Able to own a technical scope independently and communicate progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly.

  • Rigorous approach to verification, documentation, and design traceability.

  • Comfortable collaborating across disciplines and adapting to evolving product requirements.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to operate autonomously in a fast-growing company.

  • High integrity and professionalism in handling sensitive defense technologies.

jobs.title: FPGA Engineer - Radar
jobs.description:
FPGA Engineer - Radar

About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

Role & Mission

  • Turn radar sensing requirements into FPGA designs that support reliable drone detection in operational conditions.

  • Define how radar data is acquired, processed, and delivered to the rest of the system, working across RF, electronics, and software teams.

  • Establish processing budgets and select implementation approaches based on detection performance, latency, numerical accuracy, and available FPGA resources.

  • Develop reference models to study radar behavior in noise and clutter and guide hardware design decisions.

  • Build reusable RTL functions for waveform generation and receive processing in FMCW and pulsed radar systems.

  • Implement the processing stages needed to extract targets from radar returns, including matched filtering, pulse compression, range-Doppler processing, clutter rejection, and CFAR detection.

  • Integrate ADC/DAC interfaces, coordinate transmit and receive timing, and ensure synchronization with the radar front end.

  • Specify how detections and associated measurements are passed to tracking functions and embedded software.

  • Verify designs against reference models through automated testbenches and hardware-in-the-loop testing.

  • Investigate performance gaps on target hardware and use laboratory measurements and field results to improve the processing chain.

  • Document design decisions, interfaces, and validation results to support integration and future product development.


Candidate Profile

  • At least three years of FPGA development experience, with practical exposure to radar or sonar processing.

  • Ability to take a signal-processing function from an algorithmic description to verified RTL in VHDL or Verilog/SystemVerilog.

  • Strong DSP foundations, including FFT, digital filtering, windowing, and the effects of quantization and fixed-point precision.

  • Understanding of how radar systems estimate target range and velocity, distinguish returns from clutter, and set detection thresholds.

  • Working knowledge of matched filtering, pulse compression, range-Doppler maps, and CFAR techniques.

  • Familiarity with FMCW and pulsed radar, including the relationship between waveform choices, acquisition timing, and digital processing.

  • Experience assessing radar performance through simulation, including signal-to-noise ratio and clutter effects.

  • Experience developing testbenches, debugging FPGA hardware, and validating processing chains with hardware-in-the-loop methods.

  • Master’s degree or equivalent in Electrical Engineering, Signal Processing, Applied Physics, or a related field.

Skills & Qualities

  • Hands-on engineer motivated by making radar processing work reliably on physical hardware.

  • Able to connect system-level performance issues with their causes in algorithms, RTL, interfaces, or timing.

  • Methodical approach to debugging, verification, and documenting technical decisions.

  • Comfortable owning development tasks and coordinating integration work across disciplines.

  • Clear communicator who makes trade-offs explicit and flags risks early.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to operate autonomously in a fast-growing company.

  • High integrity and professionalism in handling sensitive defense technologies.

jobs.description:
Enseignante Chercheuse ou Enseignant Chercheur (Maître de conférences) BIM et Performance Durable des Bâtiments en CDI à IMT Nord Europe

INTITULÉ : « BIM et Performance Durable des Bâtiments ».

SPÉCIALITÉS : « Génie civil, BIM, Matériaux de construction durables, Performance des bâtiments ».

ÉTABLISSEMENT D'AFFECTATION :

École Nationale Supérieure Mines-Télécom Lille Douai dont le nom d'usage est IMT Nord Europe.

Direction / Service : Centre d'Enseignement, de Recherche et d'Innovation Matériaux & Procédés (CERI MP)

Responsable hiérarchique : Directeur du CERI Matériaux & Procédés

Catégorie : Agent de catégorie A ou contractuel cadre de gestion de catégorie II

Nature du poste : CDI

Lieu de travail : Site de Douai. Des déplacements sur les autres sites de l'École et auprès des partenaires sont à prévoir

CONTEXTE

École sous tutelle du ministère de l'économie, des finances et de la souveraineté industrielle et numérique, et école de l'Institut Mines Télécom, IMT Nord Europe a 3 missions principales : former des ingénieurs responsables aptes à résoudre les grandes problématiques du XXIème siècle ; mener des recherches débouchant sur des innovations à haute valeur ajoutée ; soutenir le développement des territoires notamment en facilitant l'innovation et les créations d'entreprises. Son objectif est de former les ingénieurs de demain, maîtrisant à la fois les technologies numériques et les savoir-faire industriels. Idéalement située au carrefour de l'Europe, à 1 heure de Paris, 30 minutes de Bruxelles et 1h30 de Londres, IMT Nord Europe a l'ambition de devenir un acteur majeur des grandes transformations industrielles, numériques et environnementales du XXIème siècle en combinant, tant dans ses enseignements et que dans sa recherche, les sciences de l'ingénieur et les technologies du digital.

Localisée sur 2 sites principaux d'enseignement et de recherche, à Lille et à Douai, IMT Nord Europe s'appuie sur plus de 20 000m² de laboratoire pour développer un enseignement de haut niveau et une recherche d'excellence dans les domaines suivants :

•      Énergie Environnement

•      Systèmes Numériques

•      Matériaux et Procédés

L'École dispose également d'antennes à Dunkerque, Valenciennes et Alençon.

Pour plus de détails, consulter le site internet de l'Ecole : www.imt-nord-europe.fr

Le poste est à pourvoir au sein du CERI Matériaux & Procédés (CERI MP), centre de recherche positionné sur le déploiement de nouveaux matériaux et procédés nécessaires aux transitions écologiques et industrielles. Le CERI MP développe notamment des compétences en génie civil, éco-matériaux, économie circulaire, matériaux biosourcés et géosourcés, recyclage, valorisation des déchets, durabilité des matériaux, essais multi-physiques, modélisation et procédés numériques.

Dans un contexte de transformation du secteur de la construction, le BIM constitue un levier majeur pour concevoir, construire, exploiter, réhabiliter et déconstruire les bâtiments de manière plus durable. Le recrutement vise à renforcer l'offre de formation d'IMT Nord Europe dans le domaine du BIM et à développer une activité de recherche originale à l'interface entre la maquette numérique, la connaissance des matériaux, l'éco-conception, l'économie circulaire et la performance globale des bâtiments sur l'ensemble de leur cycle de vie.

Dans ce cadre, IMT Nord Europe recrute un Enseignant Chercheur ou une Enseignante Chercheuse dont les missions sont décrites ci-après.

MISSIONS :

Sous l'autorité du directeur du CERI Matériaux & Procédés, le ou la titulaire du poste aura pour mission de développer des enseignements et des activités de recherche dans le domaine du BIM appliqué aux performances durables des bâtiments. Il ou elle contribuera à former des ingénieurs capables d'utiliser la maquette numérique et les données du bâtiment pour concevoir, optimiser, suivre et améliorer les performances des ouvrages, depuis la phase de conception jusqu'à l'exploitation, la rénovation, la déconstruction et la valorisation des matériaux en fin de vie.

Le poste s'inscrit dans une logique d'intégration formation-recherche-innovation. Il devra permettre de créer un lien fort entre les compétences du CERI MP en matériaux de construction durables, procédés, recyclage et valorisation matière, et les besoins émergents du secteur du bâtiment en matière de BIM, d'openBIM, d'analyse du cycle de vie, de pilotage de la performance et d'aide à la décision.

•      Contribuer au développement et à l'animation des enseignements en BIM, matériaux durables et performance des bâtiments dans les formations d'ingénieur et de master ;

•      Développer une activité de recherche sur l'amélioration des performances des bâtiments sur leur cycle de vie, en intégrant les dimensions matériaux, environnementales, économiques et d'exploitation.

Activités d'enseignement :

La personne recrutée participera aux cours, TD, TP, projets et encadrements dans le parcours Génie Civil Environnement, le DNM ADMODC – Advanced Design and Management of Durable Constructions, ainsi que dans les enseignements liés au BIM, aux matériaux durables et aux performances des bâtiments. Elle pourra également intervenir dans d'autres formations de l'école, en formation initiale, apprentissage ou formation continue, selon les besoins pédagogiques.

•      Concevoir, assurer et faire évoluer des enseignements de niveau ingénieur et master sur les fondamentaux du BIM, la maquette numérique, l'openBIM, l'IFC, la coordination BIM et le management de l'information ;

•      Développer des enseignements appliqués liant BIM, matériaux de construction, éco-conception, analyse du cycle de vie, indicateurs carbone, performance énergétique, performance environnementale et durabilité des ouvrages ;

•      Mettre en place des TD et TP mobilisant : modélisation BIM, extraction et structuration de données, couplage BIM-simulation, BIM-ACV, gestion des informations matériaux, scénarios de rénovation et de fin de vie ;

•      Encadrer des projets intégrateurs permettant aux élèves de travailler en équipe sur un bâtiment réel ou un cas industriel : conception collaborative, choix des matériaux, estimation des impacts, suivi des performances et stratégie de valorisation matière ;

•      Participer à l'encadrement de stages, projets de fin d'études, alternants, projets de recherche et travaux d'étudiants en lien avec les entreprises et les plateformes expérimentales du CERI MP ;

•      Contribuer à l'amélioration continue des maquettes pédagogiques, à l'approche par compétences et à la cohérence avec les attendus de la formation d'ingénieur.

Activités de recherche et de transfert de technologie :

La personne recrutée développera, au sein du CERI MP, une activité de recherche portant sur l'amélioration des performances durables des bâtiments sur l'ensemble de leur cycle de vie, en s'appuyant sur le BIM comme support d'intégration, de structuration et d'exploitation des données relatives aux matériaux, aux procédés, aux usages et aux performances.

•      Développer des méthodes permettant d'enrichir les maquettes BIM avec des données matériaux fiables : propriétés mécaniques, thermiques, hydriques, environnementales, durabilité, vieillissement, réparabilité, potentiel de réemploi et recyclabilité ;

•      Intégrer l'éco-conception dans les processus BIM à travers l'aide au choix des matériaux, l'analyse de solutions constructives bas carbone, l'évaluation multicritère et le couplage avec l'analyse du cycle de vie et l'analyse des coûts sur le cycle de vie ;

•      Construire des approches numériques pour optimiser le recyclage, le réemploi et la valorisation matière en fin de vie des bâtiments, notamment via des inventaires BIM, des passeports matériaux, la traçabilité des ressources et des scénarios de déconstruction sélective ;

•      Prendre en compte la performance réelle des bâtiments pendant leur exploitation en reliant les données BIM aux données de monitoring, de capteurs, de GTB/GTC, de maintenance, d'usage et de consommation ;

•      Traiter les questions d'interopérabilité, de qualité et de gouvernance des données : formats IFC, openBIM, bases de données matériaux, ontologies, modèles de données, tableaux de bord d'indicateurs et aide à la décision ;

•      Valoriser les moyens expérimentaux du CERI MP pour produire des données matériaux utiles aux modèles numériques, aux maquettes BIM et aux outils d'aide au choix des solutions constructives durables ;

•      Publier les résultats dans des revues et conférences reconnues et contribuer à l'encadrement de doctorants, post-doctorants, ingénieurs, stagiaires de master et projets de fin d'études recherche.

Recherche partenariale, innovation et valorisation :

Un volet important du poste portera sur le développement de collaborations avec les acteurs industriels et territoriaux de la construction durable. La personne recrutée devra contribuer à faire émerger des projets de recherche appliquée, des démonstrateurs et des cas d'usage en lien avec les besoins du secteur.

•      Développer des partenariats avec les entreprises du BTP, bureaux d'études, maîtres d'ouvrage, maîtres d'œuvre, exploitants de bâtiments, industriels des matériaux, plateformes de recyclage, acteurs de la déconstruction et éditeurs ou intégrateurs de solutions BIM ;

•      Monter et piloter des projets collaboratifs : thèses CIFRE, projets régionaux, ADEME, ANR, Horizon Europe, Interreg, chaires industrielles, prestations de recherche et démonstrateurs pédagogiques ou technologiques ;

•      Contribuer à la réponse aux appels à projets, à la rédaction de livrables scientifiques et techniques, à la valorisation des résultats et au transfert vers les entreprises et les collectivités ;

•      Participer à des réseaux académiques et professionnels dans les domaines du BIM, de la construction durable, de l'économie circulaire, des matériaux bas carbone et de la performance du bâtiment.

Contribution à la vie de l'école :

•      Participer aux jurys, soutenances, conseils pédagogiques, actions de promotion, forums, journées portes ouvertes et événements de valorisation scientifique ;

•      Contribuer à la dynamique collective du CERI MP, aux actions transversales avec les autres centres de recherche et aux démarches qualité de l'École ;

•      Accompagner les étudiants dans leur professionnalisation, leur ouverture aux enjeux environnementaux et leur capacité à travailler dans des environnements collaboratifs et numériques.


PROFIL : (Prérequis/ Diplôme)

Le poste s'adresse à une personne titulaire d'un doctorat en génie civil, bâtiment durable, BIM/construction numérique, sciences et ingénierie des matériaux, performance énergétique et environnementale des bâtiments, sciences des données appliquées à la construction, ou dans un domaine proche. Une Habilitation à Diriger des Recherches, une expérience postdoctorale, une expérience d'enseignement en école d'ingénieurs ou une expérience industrielle dans le secteur de la construction constitueront des atouts.

Le profil recherché devra combiner une culture scientifique solide, une capacité à enseigner à des élèves ingénieurs et une volonté de construire un programme de recherche partenarial à l'interface entre BIM, matériaux durables, économie circulaire et performance du bâtiment.

Savoir-être :

•      Goût pour l'enseignement et l'accompagnement des élèves ;

•      Capacité à travailler en équipe pluridisciplinaire ;

•      Autonomie, rigueur scientifique et sens de l'organisation ;

•      Capacité d'écoute et de dialogue avec les partenaires industriels ;

•      Esprit d'initiative, créativité et orientation projet ;

•      Sensibilité forte aux enjeux de transition écologique.

Savoir-faire :

•      Concevoir et animer des cours, TD, TP et projets BIM ;

•      Encadrer stages, PFE, alternants, doctorants et projets de recherche ;

•      Monter et piloter des projets collaboratifs avec des entreprises ;

•      Structurer des données BIM et les relier à des indicateurs de performance ;

•      Valoriser des résultats par publications, rapports, démonstrateurs et communications ;

•      Travailler en français et en anglais.

Connaissances :

•      BIM, openBIM, IFC, maquette numérique et coordination BIM ;

•      Matériaux de construction durables, bas carbone, bio/géosourcés, recyclés ;

•      Éco-conception, analyse du cycle de vie, indicateurs carbone et coûts sur cycle de vie ;

•      Réemploi, recyclage, valorisation matière et déconstruction sélective ;

•      Performance énergétique, environnementale et hygrothermique des bâtiments.

La maîtrise d'outils ou environnements tels que Revit, Archicad, Tekla, Navisworks, Solibri, Dynamo, Grasshopper, Rhino, eveBIM, logiciels ACV, logiciels de simulation énergétique, bases IFC, Python ou bases de données sera appréciée. Le recrutement privilégiera toutefois la capacité à construire une vision scientifique et pédagogique du BIM plutôt qu'une expertise limitée à un outil logiciel.

La résidence administrative est fixée à Douai. Des déplacements sont à prévoir sur les autres sites de l'école et auprès des partenaires.

jobs.description:
Associate Account Manager (Paris)
The AI-powered OS for beauty,
wellness and self-care

About Fresha

Fresha is the AI-powered operating system for the global beauty, wellness and self-care industry, connecting and powering everything from salons and barbers to spas, medspas, fitness studios and health practices.

Trusted by millions of consumers and businesses worldwide. Fresha is used by 140,000+ businesses and 450,000+ stylists and professionals worldwide, processing over 1 billion appointments to date.

The company is headquartered in London, United Kingdom, with 15 global offices located across North America, EMEA and APAC.
Fresha allows consumers to discover, book and pay for beauty and wellness appointments with local businesses via its marketplace, while beauty and wellness businesses and professionals use an all-in-one platform to manage their entire operations with an intuitive business software and financial technology solutions.
 
Fresha’s ecosystem gives merchants everything they need to run their business seamlessly by facilitating appointment bookings, point-of-sale, customer records management, marketing automation, loyalty, beauty products inventory and team management.
 
The consumer marketplace unlocks revenue potential for partner businesses by leveraging the power of online bookings and automated marketing through mobile apps and advanced integrations with major tech brands including Instagram, Facebook and Google.

Role overview
 
Given our exciting and progressive growth plans, we are looking for an exceptional Associate Account Manager to come and join our global business.
 
Reporting directly to the Account Manager Team Lead, you will be accountable for building relationships and driving monetisation of the Fresha platform.
 
This is a great opportunity for someone looking to work in a fast-paced and changing environment, who likes to work autonomously, enjoys a challenge, and wants to make an impact.
 
To foster a collaborative environment that thrives on face-to-face interactions and teamwork, all Fresha employees work from office five days per week in Paris, on the Champs-élysées.

Commercial Growth

  • Sales Cycle - Proactively introduce, educate and convert Partners on to Fresha’s payments solution.
  • Market Trends - Optimise listing content and availability competitiveness on the marketplace to maximise conversions.

    • Relationship Building

  • Relationships - Build key internal relationships with our Sales and Onboarding teams to ensure smooth transition and handover of Partners through the Partner journey.
  • Collaboration  - Collaborate with our Product teams to provide important product feedback to help enhance future releases.
  • Persuasion - Use consultative sales techniques to understand customer needs and requirements and have the ability to upsell and cross-sell the Fresha Platform.
    •  
  • This list is not exhaustive and there may be other activities you are required to deliver. 

    • What we are looking for
  • Experience - 1-2 Years experience in effectively delivering commercial outcomes from a previous Account Management role
  • Closing Skills – Demonstrated ability to effectively close deals, negotiate, and convert opportunities
  • Adaptability - Shown to be commercially motivated with an ability to adapt and achieve targets
  • Analytics - Proven experience in using and analysing data and reporting effectively to improve commercial outcomes
  • Curiosity - Naturally proactive and inquisitive, with a desire to consistently learn and improve
  • Tele-prospecting - Previous experience in an outbound call environment or a related sales position preferred
  • Communication - Excellent and proven written, verbal and presentation skills
  • Innovative - Creative thinking and problem-solving mindset
  • Relationship Building - You are a true hunter and relationship builder
  • Team Player - Happy to roll sleeves up and assist the team when required
  • Initiative - Ability to self-starter with a proactive approach

    • Added Bonus
  • Bi-lingual - Fluency in English and another language
  • Beauty & Wellness - Experience within the beauty and wellness industry
    •  
  • At Fresha, we value passion and potential as much as specific skills. If you're enthusiastic and eager to learn, we encourage you to apply, even if you don't meet every listed requirement. We believe in fostering growth and providing the support needed for you to excel in your role.

    • Interview Process
  • Screen Call - Video-call with a member from the Talent Team (30 mins)
  • Skills & Experience - In-Person interview with Team Leads (30 mins)
  • Presentation - In-Person interview with General Manager.
    •  
    We aim to complete the entire interview process and deliver feedback within 2 weeks. 
     
  • Every job application received is reviewed manually by our talent team. While we strive to assess applications within 7 days, the sheer volume of talented individuals expressing interest may occasionally extend this timeframe

    At Fresha, we are creating a culture where individuals of all backgrounds feel comfortable.

    We do not discriminate based on race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, gender identity, national origin, disability, or any other applicable legally protected characteristics in the location in which the candidate is applying.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - Device Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Member of Technical Staff - Device Software Engineer

Technology that speaks your language

Domera Labs builds Ami, the first AI companion for seniors. Ami brings the power of a smartphone into a more human form: voice-first and deeply personalized

We at Domera Labs are rethinking human-machine interaction from first principles by introducing a better interface to interact with technology: voice

By combining the most intuitive hardware design with frontier AI, Ami makes AI accessible for the fastest growing demographic worldwide. The goal is to make the everyday life older adults more seamless, while addressing that generation's biggest challenge: loneliness and isolation. With Ami we are building the category leader of a new hardware paradigm by building a full standalone device (and not a gadget) that aims to makes the smartphones of today redundant.

The underlying technology of Ami combines a model-agnostic streaming pipeline consisting of proprietary models and off-the-shelf frontier models to create a hyper-personalized and proactive user experience. The backbone of Ami is built by our foundational lab that builds a social intelligence model that is optimized for social interaction, human behavior and interpersonal skills.

Domera Labs has secured large distribution agreements, a model co-development partnership with a leading AI lab, and ODM manufacturing proposals. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of human-machine interaction, mass-consumer facing hardware and shape frontier research with social/non-quantifiable benchmarking.


Core Responsibilities

You own the software that makes Ami work. Your primary responsibility is to architect, write and ship the on-device application and services for our mass-market consumer device, from voice interaction and cloud connectivity to onboarding, recovery and everyday reliability. You will work directly with our ODM and silicon partners to integrate that software with the underlying platform.

Our target hardware uses a Qualcomm SoC with Android/AOSP or embedded Linux depending on the final platform selection.

Our users are 75 years old and there is no screen, no settings menu, and no IT support. If the device does not work out of the box, it fails. Your job is to make the following work.

  • On-device application: build and own Ami's application and services, including interaction logic, real-time audio streaming, cloud communication, local state and recovery from network interruptions or service failures

  • Device identity and fleet management: provisioning, unique device identity, secure key storage, and the systems that let us know what every unit in the field is doing

  • The maintenance channel: a reliable service and diagnostics path to the device (BLE, USB-C, or both) for field debugging, factory test, and recovery

  • Out-of-the-box experience: first-boot network onboarding that a senior can complete alone, with no screen and no smartphone as a crutch. This is the single highest-stakes piece of the product

  • Flash and update management: partition layout, A/B OTA with rollback, staged fleet rollouts, and bricking as a category of bug that never happens

  • Base platform behaviors: boot and recovery, factory and soft resets, button and LED mappings, audio feedback, power states and battery behavior

  • The audio front end: working with our ODM and silicon partners on mic array, echo cancellation, wake word, and the latency budget from mic to first spoken token

  • Bringing the device through EVT, DVT, and PVT with our ODM as the technical counterpart on our side

 

What we are looking for

Das Unternehmen bietet End-to-End-Lösungen zum Schutz von Wohn- und Geschäftsobjekten jeder Größenordnung. Bis heute umfasst das Produktportfolio von Ajax 280 Geräte für Einbruchschutz, Videoüberwachung, Brand- und Lebenssicherheit sowie Komfort- und Automatisierungslösungen. Das Unternehmen beschäftigt 5.000 Spezialisten.

Wir bauen lokale Teams auf, weil wir davon überzeugt sind, dass lokale Experten die Besonderheiten ihres Marktes am besten verstehen. Ajax Systems ist weltweit mit Vertriebsmitarbeitern vertreten, unter anderem in Norwegen, Schweden, Dänemark, Finnland, Italien, Spanien, Deutschland, Frankreich, dem Vereinigten Königreich, den USA, Australien, Südafrika und weiteren Regionen. Das globale Business-Development-Team vereint Gleichgesinnte, die die ambitionierten Ziele von Ajax Systems teilen.

Die Kombination aus erstklassiger Software und leistungsstarker Hardware hat die Wahrnehmung von Sicherheitssystemen für Anwender und Branchenexperten nachhaltig verändert. Durch Anerkennungen auf den größten Fachmessen wie IFSEC, Expoprotection und Intersec sowie durch den Gewinn renommierter Auszeichnungen führender Branchenmedien wie dem PSI Magazine und GIT SECURITY zählt Ajax heute zu den meistausgezeichneten Sicherheitssystemen Europas.

Der Business Development Manager von Ajax Systems soll daher als Botschafter des Unternehmens und der Marke fungieren und die folgenden Aufgaben erfüllen:

  • Werbung für die Produkte und Dienstleistungen von Ajax Systems bei Systemintegratoren, Errichtern, Fachberatern und Endverbrauchern (Geschäftspartnern) in Deutschland.
  • Erkundung neuer Geschäftsmöglichkeiten und Organisation von Treffen mit Geschäftspartnern.

jobs.description:
Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Planning & Navigation)

Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will make our robots navigate dependably across real customer sites. Our stack works. The gap between working and dependable is the whole job. Every new site tests how a robot understands its surroundings and chooses where to go: a ramp the planner avoids, a narrow passage that exposes a poor route, a gate that changes the map, a person who steps into the robot's path, or localization drift that builds over a long patrol. You treat those cases as the real navigation problem to solve, not as edge cases.

You'll shape the technical choices behind reliable navigation, from sensor selection, ground segmentation, and traversability estimation to predicting how people and vehicles move and planning safe, efficient routes around them. The system has to work day and night, in challenging weather, across different embodiments and changing site conditions. We measure success by whether the robot completes its patrol on a live site, not by how it performs in simulation.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

  • Navigation and path-planning design: how robots represent traversable space, select routes, avoid obstacles, and reach goals across complex sites.

  • Sensor integration driven by navigation requirements, including what ground segmentation and traversability estimation need in day, night, and challenging weather.

  • Environment understanding: how the robot distinguishes ground from obstacles and estimates which terrain is safe and practical to traverse.

  • Behavior prediction: anticipate how people, vehicles, and other dynamic obstacles will move, and plan routes that stay safe and efficient around them.

  • Field reliability: reproduce failures from deployments, find the root cause, and fix it at the right layer, from sensor data and maps to costmaps, planners, and recovery behaviors.

  • Planning under imperfect localization: plans that stay useful when the state estimate drifts and the robot must execute routes in tight or dynamic environments, working with the rest of Robot Autonomy on localization and control.

  • Validation on real robots: logs, simulation, and repeatable field tests to verify that design choices and changes hold across routes, lighting, weather, and site layouts.

  • New autonomy capabilities: work with the engineers building the operator application and backend so operator requests and new robot capabilities rest on a sound navigation design.

  • The field feedback loop: work closely with forward-deployed engineers to turn site issues into bugs, design changes, and improvements to the navigation stack.

  • Regular site visits to build a practical understanding of how robots and sensors behave in real operating conditions.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for an engineer who has taken a robotics system from unreliable to dependable and takes ownership beyond individual tickets. You can explain why you made a navigation design choice and what it costs. When a robot takes a bad route, you can tell whether the planner, the map, the state estimate, or the robot's behavior is at fault, and you fix the right one. You are comfortable in the field and want to understand how robots behave in real customer environments.

YOUR BACKGROUND:

  • A Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Proven track record building and deploying navigation on ground mobile robots in the real world (3+ years or equivalent depth).

  • Hands-on experience with mobile robot navigation and path planning: route or local planning, static and dynamic obstacle avoidance, costmaps, or recovery behaviors.

  • Understanding of how mapping and localization affect navigation, and the ability to diagnose when a planning issue is actually caused by the map, the state estimate, or robot behavior.

  • Understanding of how lighting, weather, terrain, and sensor limitations affect perception and navigation, with experience developing or validating systems for demanding real-world conditions.

  • Hands-on experience with robotics sensors and hardware, especially LiDAR, IMUs, and cameras. You can investigate issues across software, networking, and hardware boundaries.

  • Experience testing and debugging navigation on physical robots using logs, visualization, simulation, and repeatable field tests.

  • Strong ROS 2, C++, and Python skills.

  • Clear communication of navigation and path-planning design choices and their trade-offs.

  • Willingness to visit customer sites regularly.

NICE TO HAVE:

  • Experience with legged robots or with more than one robot embodiment.

  • Experience with Nav2 or a comparable navigation framework.

  • Motion prediction or planning among people and vehicles, such as trajectory forecasting or socially aware navigation.

  • Terrain mapping and traversability methods: elevation mapping, learned traversability, or semantic segmentation for navigation.

  • Experience with night-time or all-weather sensing, such as thermal cameras or LiDAR in rain and fog.

  • Background in security, defence, or other safety-critical robotics deployments.

What We Offer

  • Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

  • Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

  • Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

  • Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

  • Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

jobs.title: Technical Pre-sales Solution Engineer (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
Technical Pre-sales Solution Engineer (f/m/d)

Role Overview

As a Technical Pre-sales Solution Engineer (EMS, PPC & SCADA) at NeuVerge-Tron GmbH, you will serve as the technical lead and solution architect during pre-sales and tender phases for utility-scale renewable energy and energy storage power plants.

In this position, your core product portfolio comprises Energy Management Systems (EMS), Power Plant Controllers (PPC), and SCADA platforms. You will analyze customer requirements, regional Grid Codes, and Transmission/Distribution System Operator (TSO/DSO) mandates, translating them into resilient, high-availability, and cybersecure system architectures.

(Note: This role focuses on control software, industrial automation, and OT system architecture; it does not cover battery cell sizing, containerized mechanical design, or civil EPC scope.)

 

Key Responsibilities

Technical Pre-sales & Bid Management

  • Analyze customer technical specifications, RFIs, RFQs, and RFPs for utility-scale solar, wind, and hybrid BESS assets.

  • Author technical proposals, functional architecture diagrams, and Statements of Work (SOW) for EMS/SCADA solutions.

  • Compile compliance matrices and deviation lists addressing customer specifications and utility regulations.

  • Define the Bill of Materials (BOM), covering server hardware, industrial controllers, networking equipment, software licenses, and engineering services.

  • Lead technical deep-dive workshops, solution demonstrations, and clarification sessions with customers, EPC contractors, and grid operators.

Grid Code Compliance & Functional Control Design

  • Evaluate regional Grid Code regulations across target European markets (e.g., VDE-AR-N 4110/4120, ENTSO-E standards) and translate them into EMS/PPC control requirements

  • Architect plant-level control logic, including Active Power Control, Reactive Power/Power Factor Regulation, POI/PCC Voltage Support, Frequency Response, and Ramp Rate restrictions.

  • Define EMS-level operational strategies, such as automated dispatch tracking, State of Charge (SoC) management constraints, energy arbitrage scheduling, ancillary service controls, and fail-safe/black-start logics.

System Integration & Communication Architecture

  • Design overall system architectures connecting EMS, PPC, SCADA, Historian, and Human-Machine Interfaces (HMI).

  • Define interface specifications for external subsystems: Battery Management Systems (BMS), Power Conversion Systems (PCS), MV switchgear, digital protection relays, power meters, and TSO/DSO dispatch centers.

  • Develop and maintain interface control documents (ICD), data point lists, and signal mapping registers.

  • Implement and validate standard industrial protocols, including Modbus TCP/RTU, IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850 (MMS/GOOSE), DNP3, and OPC UA.

  • Architect high-availability schemes, redundancy topologies, automated failover mechanisms, time synchronization (NTP/PTP), and disaster recovery plans.

OT Networking & Cybersecurity Architecture

  • Design Operational Technology (OT) network topologies, VLAN segmentations, IP addressing schemes, and DMZ firewall policies.

  • Formulate secure remote maintenance topologies, jump host concepts, VPN tunnels, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) mechanisms.

  • Ensure EMS solution adherence to cybersecurity standards, including IEC 62443 and IEC 62351 frameworks.

  • Collaborate with customer IT/OT security teams and external auditors during security reviews and threat modeling assessments.

Verification & Handover

  • Define verification scopes and technical criteria for Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), and grid compliance commissioning.

  • Support engineering, commissioning, and project management teams during post-award handover to ensure seamless project delivery.

 

Scope Boundaries

  • To preserve focus on control systems and software integration, this position explicitly excludes:

  • Battery cell/module selection, chemistry evaluation, and electrochemical degradation modeling.

  • Mechanical layout, thermal HVAC design, or fire suppression engineering of BESS containers.

  • Primary high/medium voltage electrical hardware engineering (transformers, switchgear internals, or EPC civil infrastructure).

 

Qualifications & Profile

Education:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Automation, Power Systems, Computer Engineering, or a related engineering discipline.

Professional Experience:

  • 3 to 5+ years of experience in technical presales, solution architecture, or systems engineering focusing on EMS, PPC, or SCADA in power generation or grid utilities.

  • Practical familiarity with grid integration procedures and technical dialogue with European grid operators (TSOs/DSOs).

Technical & Protocol Competencies:

  • Solid understanding of power utility communication standards: IEC 60870-5-104, IEC 61850, Modbus TCP/RTU, DNP3, and OPC UA.

  • Hands-on experience with industrial automation platforms (PLCs/RTUs), real-time historians, and SCADA packages.

  • Working knowledge of industrial cybersecurity best practices (IEC 62443 / IEC 62351).

Key Competencies:

  • Strong analytical capability to dissect technical tender documents into structured requirements.

  • Confident presentation skills in customer-facing technical exchanges and contract negotiations.

Language Skills:

  • Professional fluency in English (written and verbal) is required.

  • German language or any other third EU or Chinese proficiency are strongly preferred.

jobs.title: Propulsion Engineer
jobs.description:
Propulsion Engineer

Propulsion Engineer - Solid Rocket Motors

We are looking for a Propulsion Engineer to support the design, development, manufacture, testing, and qualification of the solid rocket motors used on our orbital launch vehicle. This is a hands-on role covering the full motor development cycle, from preliminary design through static-fire testing and flight qualification.

 

You will work as part of the project team delivering an orbital-class launch vehicle, contributing to the development of propulsion hardware, engineering analysis, test campaigns, and the tools required to support motor and vehicle-level design.

 

About us

We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications.

 

We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, generating significant revenue and applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket.

 

We are working hard to build something truly spectacular.

 

To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you.

 

Key responsibilities

  • Contribute to the design and development of solid rocket motors from preliminary design through detailed design, manufacturing readiness, static-fire testing, and flight qualification.

  • Perform engineering analysis covering relevant aspects of internal ballistics, grain geometry, motor performance, nozzle design, motor cases, and structural sizing.

  • Develop or extend Python-based analysis and simulation tools for ballistic simulation, performance prediction, structural sizing, and related design activities.

  • Translate vehicle-level performance requirements—including total impulse, burn time, thrust profile, and mass fraction—into motor-level design specifications.

  • Feed measured motor performance data back into vehicle-level design and sizing tools.

  • Support the definition and execution of verification and validation activities, including analysis, subscale and component testing, static-fire testing, and flight qualification.

  • Support the planning and execution of static-fire test campaigns, including instrumentation requirements, test preparation, and post-test data analysis.

  • Prepare technical documentation, design reviews, test plans, analysis reports, and clear records of design assumptions and results.

  • Work closely with structures, manufacturing, chemistry, systems, and vehicle engineering teams to manage interfaces and cross-disciplinary design impacts.

  • Contribute to the development of engineering methods, tools, and processes as the propulsion team and company scale.

 

What we are looking for

  • A Bachelor's or Master's degree in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related discipline.

  • Experience or demonstrated academic/project experience in solid rocket motor design, propulsion, aerospace hardware, experimental engineering, or a closely related field.

  • An understanding of several propulsion disciplines, including internal ballistics, grain design, nozzle design, motor case design, or propulsion performance.

  • A strong foundation in thermodynamics and internal ballistics, including combustion, propellant energetics, and burn-rate behaviour.

  • Working knowledge of nozzle flow theory and thrust coefficient behaviour, including off-design and altitude effects.

  • Working knowledge of pressure-vessel and composite structural design principles.

  • Proficiency in Python or a similar programming language for developing and maintaining engineering analysis tools.

  • An understanding of verification and validation approaches for propulsion hardware.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work from first principles when established methods or tools do not exist.

  • The ability to work independently, take responsibility for assigned technical work, and contribute effectively within a small, fast-moving team.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to document design assumptions, analysis, and results clearly for a cross-disciplinary team.

 

Desirable experience

  • Direct experience designing, manufacturing, assembling, or testing solid rocket motors.

  • Experience with composite filament-winding process design or qualification.

  • Experience supporting or executing static-fire test campaigns.

  • Experience analysing pressure, force, temperature, or other propulsion test instrumentation data.

  • Propellant formulation or strand-burner testing experience.

  • Experience with explosives licensing, range safety, or similar regulatory processes for propellant systems.

  • Experience at an early-stage aerospace company or in a similar environment.

  • Familiarity with vehicle-level launch-vehicle design, including staging, mass budgeting, performance sizing, or trajectory analysis.

Benefits and important information:

  • We offer top-decile compensation packages, bonuses and meaningful equity, to attract exceptional aerospace talent.

  • Every employee is awarded stock options in the company, you will directly benefit from your own hard work and success.

  • Comprehensive relocation support including flights, shipping and visas.

  • Lunch, dinner and drinks provided everyday

  • Free access to shared company housing

Please note, we are a fast paced, hyper-scaling startup. You will need to be comfortable working extended hours with high levels of autonomy, ownership, and flexibility, with contracts structured around a 48-hour working week.

We are committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, has equal access to opportunity, and can thrive. We welcome different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences—and believe our differences make us stronger.

  • Love Brand aufbauen. Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit uns eine globale Love Brand für B2C und B2B und prägst mit, wie StudySmarter aussieht und klingt.


Was die Rolle nicht ist

  • Keine klassische Designstelle. Geschmack und Markenurteil sind wichtig, die handwerkliche Ausführung läuft über AI und Freelancer.
  • Kein Performance-Marketing-Job. Kanäle, Budget, Bidding und Attribution liegen an anderer Stelle im Team.
  • Keine Briefing-Rolle. Du machst die Arbeit selbst, statt sie weiterzugeben.
  • Keine Product-Rolle. Du bist kein Product Manager. Du trägst die Nutzerakquisition und arbeitest dafür eng mit dem Product Team zusammen, ohne Produktverantwortung zu übernehmen.
  • Keine Führungsrolle. Du arbeitest eng im Marketing-Team und gemeinsam mit dem Gründerteam, führst aber keine eigenen Mitarbeitenden. Dafür deutlich mehr Gestaltungsspielraum.


Was du für diese Rolle brauchst

  • Starke AI-Skills. Du arbeitest täglich mit AI-Tools wie Claude Code, Codex oder ähnlichen, dazu mit Agents und Automatisierung. Du baust eigene Seiten, Tools und Workflows und bringst sie selbst live, statt nur Prompts zu schreiben.
  • Starkes Copywriting und Storytelling. Du schreibst Texte, die auffallen und konvertieren, und findest die
    Worte, die bei Schülerinnen, Schülern und Studierenden ankommen. Du denkst in Geschichten und Nutzen, nicht in Feature-Listen.
  • Eigenständigkeit und Tempo. Du nimmst ein Thema und bringst es durch. Zehn Dinge live und gemessen sind Dir lieber als zwei perfekte. Zahlenverständnis. Du liest Funnel selbst, arbeitest in Analytics-Tools und bewertest Tests ehrlich, auch wenn
    das Ergebnis gegen Deine Idee spricht.
  • Ein Auge für Design. Du erkennst, was gut aussieht und was nicht, und kannst einschätzen, wann Design
    Conversion bringt und wann es nur Dekoration ist. Figma ist Dir vertraut.
  • Marketing-Grundverständnis. Du weißt, wie Paid, SEO und Lifecycle grundsätzlich funktionieren. Die Details der einzelnen Kanäle lernst Du bei uns.
Zwei Dinge sind Voraussetzung:
  • Deutsch auf Muttersprachniveau. Du schreibst für unsere Zielgruppe auf Landing Pages, in
    Ads, in den App Stores und offline. Ohne echtes Sprachgefühl funktioniert das nicht.
  • Eigene Projekte, die Du zeigen kannst. Seiten, Tools, Content, Nebenprojekte. Das sagt uns
    mehr als ein Lebenslauf.

Wir schauen auf Skills, Execution, Tempo, Kreativität und Ambition, nicht auf die Anzahl der Berufsjahre. Starke
Absolventinnen und Absolventen sind ausdrücklich willkommen, ebenso Profile mit einigen Jahren Erfahrung.


Warum StudySmarter?

  • Remote arbeiten, so viel Du möchtest
  • Modernes Büro mit Terrasse, mitten im Münchner Werksviertel
  • Beteiligung am Unternehmenserfolg
  • Ausstattung nach Deiner Wahl
  • Direkter Draht zu den Foundern
  • EGYM Wellpass für Sport und Gesundheit
  • Obst, Säfte, Porridge-Bar und Getränke-Flatrate
  • Regelmäßige Team-Events, Sommer- und
  • Weihnachtsfeier
  • Budget für Fortbildung und Weiterentwicklung
  • Ein Umfeld, in dem Du AI nicht rechtfertigen musst


Deine Bewerbung

Schick uns Deinen CV und Links zu AI-Projekten, die Du verantwortet hast. Ein Anschreiben ist optional. Und zeig uns etwas, das Du in den letzten drei Monaten mit AI gebaut hast. Ein paar Absätze oder ein kurzes Video genügen.

Wir schätzen unterschiedliche Erfahrungen und Perspektiven und ermutigen alle Menschen, sich zu
bewerben, auch wenn nicht jede Anforderung perfekt erfüllt ist. Wenn Du unsicher bist, ob Dein Profil passt,
bewirb Dich und lass es uns beurteilen.
